extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and readers of political and social science journals (academic book-review readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and standards used in academic journal book reviews for political and social science works, emphasizing scope, organization, originality, methodology, tone, and contribution to the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive subject grouping and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutes cover a wide range of subject matter and are grouped together under the following heads: Agriculture, Vocational Education, Banking, Immigration and Naturalization, Business Regulation, Food and Drugs, Labor, Taxation, Commerce, Elections, National Defense, Trade Marks and Copyrights, Moral Reform, Bankruptcy, Criminal Code, Judicial Code, Health and Roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within these groups all statutes of importance up to those passed in the early summer of 1917 are given; organization by subject-heads and inclusion of statutes of current importance are positive features of a useful compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of them have been passed or revised since 1910, showing how recent is the main body of regulative statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compilation/review should note the date-range and recency of material; inclusion of the latest statutes (up to a stated cut-off) is an important evaluative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility / administrative applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: They provide for an extensive increase in the national administrative machinery to carry out their enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators value whether the work reveals practical implications (e.g., administrative structures required) and whether it aids practitioners or administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of editorial selection and convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Lapp has performed a real service in selecting and bringing together in this convenient form the chief federal measures of present interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider how well the editor selects, curates, and presents material for convenient use by the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: International influence and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the many notable addresses delivered by Mr. Root ... certainly none have had a larger international influence than the series of remarkable speeches which he delivered during his tour through South America ... These addresses possess a significance far deeper than the mere formal greetings of a distinguished representative of the government of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book reviews should evaluate the work's influence and significance beyond immediate context, noting works with broad diplomatic or international impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and attitude toward other nations
rubrics_metrics.description: In Mr. Root's addresses there is totally absent that spirit of condescension characterizing so many American utterances; an attitude which has done much injury to our relations with Central and South America. They breathe, not only a broad patriotism, but carry to our sister republics a message of true friendship and helpfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether tone is respectful and constructive; reviews may praise absence of condescension and presence of friendship/helpfulness as virtues in diplomatic or international writings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative/definitive treatment of policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On this solemn occasion he summarized in admirable form the spirit which should dominate the relations of the American countries with one another. This one address should be read and re-read by the American people, and it is no exaggeration to say that future generations will find therein the best and highest expression of American foreign policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note if a work contains exemplary or enduring statements that synthesize or define policy and recommend them for wide readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience appropriateness / specialist focus
rubrics_metrics.description: This is another addition to the series of contributions to international law ... Inasmuch as it deals with only one of the multifarious questions of international law, it will appeal to the specialist rather than to the general student of international law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state for whom the work is intended (specialists vs general students) and evaluate suitability for that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / treatment of a previously unresearched question
rubrics_metrics.description: The author undertakes to answer a question which has never heretofore been the subject of research: What is the effect of international conventions on other states than those which are parties thereto?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight and evaluate novel research questions or coverage of neglected topics as a criterion of contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological thoroughness (use of multiple sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author reviews the principles laid down in the municipal laws of the more important states ... summarizes and criticizes the opinions of the jurists and text writers who have previously considered the subject. Finally, he examines the precedents that have arisen in diplomatic practice, and on the basis of the information obtained from these three sources, he formulates his own conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should consider whether the author uses a comprehensive, multi-source method (doctrinal law, jurist literature, practice/precedent) and whether conclusions are well founded on that evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to literature and bibliographic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Altogether the monograph throws much light on a hitherto neglected subject and as such it is a distinct contribution to the literature of international law. It contains a valuable bibliography of the authorities who have heretofore touched upon the question which he attempts to answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the work's contribution to scholarship and the usefulness of its bibliography and references for future researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of style and accessible terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The style is clear. The author knows the other writers in his field and presents their views accurately. He uses ordinary terms wherever possible and for this deserves much credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, plain language, and accurate representation of others' views are key stylistic criteria in academic book reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and comprehensiveness of subject-treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The first three chapters are introductory ... In the next five chapters the nature of social unity is discussed at length as is also social change under normal and abnormal conditions. In the succeeding chapters special topics ... are treated, the closing chapter being in reality a summary on the nature of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book's chapter structure and coverage logically develop the subject and whether topics are adequately arranged and summarized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical engagement with theoretical positions
rubrics_metrics.description: For instance the hedonistic explanation of conduct is rather lightly disposed of on the ground of the inborn activity of the organism without regard to external stimulus. I am not convinced that the problem ends there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should identify substantive theoretical treatments they find insufficiently argued and note where further evidence or reasoning is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of underlying empirical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The great question which comes to the mind is not concerned with the author's positions but has to do with the reliability of the data presented by psychology on which social psychology must be based. Here I have many doubts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the empirical foundations cited are dependable; concerns about data reliability are material to the work's overall validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and stimulation of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitting this situation, I must compliment Dr. Ellwood on his ability to select and present his material. His discussion is timely and stimulating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive criterion is whether the work provokes thought and addresses issues of current interest; such timeliness and stimulation are merits to be noted.
